title: Time
summary: Time counts in 60s, 24s and 7s, not in tens, so you can't subtract times like decimals. You'll convert units, use the [[24-hour-clock|24-hour clock]], work out how long things take, and read timetables and [[time-zone|time zones]].

goals.text: Convert between seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months and years, including parts of an hour.
Change times between the 12-hour and 24-hour clock, and read a clock face.
Work out how long something takes, and when it starts or ends, including past midnight.
Read a timetable and work out local times in other time zones.

before.prompt: Which of these is a [[multiple|multiple]] of $15$?
Write down the smallest multiple of $60$ that is bigger than $200$.
before.explain: $60, 120, 180, 240$, and $240$ is the first past $200$. Revise it in {{lesson:1.1}}.

blocks.text: Time does not count in tens. There are $60$ minutes in an hour, so $2$ hours $30$ minutes is not $2.30$ hours.

blocks.tex: 1\text{ min} = 60\text{ s} \qquad 1\text{ h} = 60\text{ min} \qquad 1\text{ day} = 24\text{ h}
1\text{ week} = 7\text{ days} \qquad 1\text{ year} = 12\text{ months} = 365\text{ days } (366 \text{ in a leap year})

blocks.text: To change to a smaller unit, multiply. To change to a bigger unit, divide.

blocks.question: Three podcast episodes last $48$, $52$ and $55$ minutes. Work out the total time, in hours and minutes.
steps: Take out whole hours: $2 \times 60 = 120$, and $180$ is too many, so $2$ hours.

blocks.text: For part of an hour, multiply by $60$: $\tfrac{1}{4}$ hour is $15$ minutes, and $0.4$ hours is $24$ minutes, not $40$.

blocks.question: A cyclist rides for $2.35$ hours. Write this time in hours and minutes.
steps: Change the rest to minutes: $0.35 \times 60 = 21$ minutes.

blocks.prompt: How many minutes are there in $2$ days?
blocks.hint: Days to hours, then hours to minutes.

blocks.prompt: How many minutes are there in $1\tfrac{3}{4}$ hours?
blocks.explain: $\tfrac{3}{4}$ of $60$ is $45$, and $60 + 45 = 105$. $135$ reads $1.75$ as $1$ hour $75$ minutes, and $175$ reads it as $175$ minutes.

blocks.prompt: Ana is $15$ years $4$ months old. Her brother is $9$ years $11$ months. Work out the difference in their ages.
blocks.hint: Swap $1$ year for $12$ months: $15$ years $4$ months is $14$ years $16$ months.
blocks.explain: $16 - 11 = 5$ months and $14 - 9 = 5$ years. $6$ years $5$ months forgets the swapped year, and $6$ years $7$ months takes $4$ from $11$.

blocks.text: The 12-hour clock uses a.m. from midnight to noon, and p.m. from noon to midnight.

blocks.statement: The [[24-hour-clock|24-hour clock]] writes a time as four digits, from $00\,00$ at midnight to $23\,59$: hours since midnight, then minutes.
blocks.plain: After noon the hours keep counting past $12$.

blocks.text: 1. a.m.: write the hour with two digits, so $7.05$ a.m. is $07\,05$. From midnight to 1 a.m. the hour is $00$.
2. p.m.: add $12$ to the hour, so $4.50$ p.m. is $16\,50$. From noon to 1 p.m. the hour stays $12$.
3. Going back: hours $01$ to $11$ are a.m., and hour $12$ is p.m. Take $12$ from hours $13$ to $23$ and write p.m. An hour of $00$ becomes $12$ a.m.
On a clock face, read the long minute hand first: each number is $5$ minutes. For the hour, take the last number the short hand has reached.

blocks.alt: Analogue clock face with the numbers 1 to 12. The long minute hand points at 10. The short hour hand is between 4 and 5, closer to 5.
blocks.caption: The hour hand is close to $5$ but has not reached it.

blocks.question: The clock in the figure shows a time in the afternoon. Write it in the 24-hour clock.
steps: The hour hand has passed $4$ but not $5$, so it is $4.50$ p.m.

blocks.question: A ferry leaves at $00\,25$. Write this time in the 12-hour clock.
steps: In the 12-hour clock that hour is $12$, and it is a.m.

blocks.hint: p.m. means add $12$ to the hour.

blocks.prompt: A shop closes at $14\,15$. Write this time in the 12-hour clock.
blocks.hint: The hour is over $12$: take $12$ away.
blocks.explain: $14 - 12 = 2$, and it is after noon: 2.15 p.m.

sections.heading: How long, and when it ends

blocks.text: To find how long something takes, count on: to the next whole hour, then whole hours, then the minutes to the end.

blocks.question: A train leaves at $08\,47$ and arrives at $13\,22$. How long is the journey, in hours and minutes?

blocks.text: Working out $13.22 - 8.47 = 4.75$ and writing $4$ h $75$ min. An hour has $60$ minutes, not $100$, so count on.
To find an end time, add the hours, then the minutes. Swap each $60$ minutes for $1$ hour. Past $24$, take away $24$: it is the next day.

blocks.question: A coach leaves at $21\,38$ on Monday. The journey takes $4$ hours $55$ minutes. Work out the day and time it arrives.
steps: Add the hours: $21 + 4 = 25$, which is $01$ on Tuesday. So $01\,38$.
Add the minutes: $38 + 55 = 93$ minutes, which is $1$ h $33$ min.

blocks.prompt: A night shift runs from $22\,40$ to $06\,15$ the next morning. How long is the shift?
blocks.explain: $1$ h $20$ min to midnight, then $6$ h $15$ min: $7$ h $35$ min. $16$ h $25$ min counts backwards.

blocks.prompt: A cake needs $1$ hour $50$ minutes in the oven, then $25$ minutes to cool. It must be ready at $16\,00$. Work out the latest time it can go in the oven.
blocks.hint: Add the two times, then work backwards from $16\,00$.
blocks.explain: $2$ h $15$ min back from $16\,00$ is $13\,45$. $14\,10$ forgets the cooling, and $13\,85$ treats an hour as $100$ minutes.

blocks.text: In a timetable, read down a column to follow one bus. Read across a row to see every bus at one stop.

blocks.alt: Bus timetable with four stops and three buses. Harbour: 06 50, 07 35, 08 20. Market Square: 07 08, 07 53, 08 38. Hospital: 07 26, 08 11, 08 56. Airport: 08 04, 08 49, 09 34.
blocks.caption: A bus leaves Harbour every $45$ minutes.

blocks.question: Use the timetable. How long does Bus B take from Harbour to the Airport?
steps: Down the Bus B column: $07\,35$ at Harbour, $08\,49$ at the Airport.

blocks.prompt: Use the timetable. Tom gets to Market Square at $07\,40$ and takes the next bus. When does he reach the Hospital?
blocks.hint: Read across the Market Square row for the first time after $07\,40$.
blocks.explain: The next bus is Bus B at $07\,53$. Down its column, it reaches the Hospital at $08\,11$.

blocks.text: Each [[time-zone|time zone]] has its own local time. Ahead means add the difference; behind means subtract it.
For a flight, add the flight time to the departure time first. Then change to local time, and check the day.

blocks.question: A plane leaves Dubai at $14\,20$ local time on Saturday. The flight to Tokyo takes $9$ hours $35$ minutes. Tokyo is $5$ hours ahead of Dubai. Work out the day and local time in Tokyo when it lands.
steps: In Dubai time: $14\,20 + 9$ h $35$ min $= 23\,55$ on Saturday.
Tokyo is ahead, so add $5$ hours: $23\,55$ becomes $28\,55$.
Past $24$, so take away $24$: $04\,55$ on Sunday.

blocks.prompt: A plane leaves London at $11\,15$ and flies for $8$ hours $20$ minutes to Toronto. Toronto is $5$ hours behind London. Work out the local time in Toronto when it lands.
blocks.hint: Add the flight time in London time, then take away $5$ hours.

blocks.text: $60$ s $= 1$ min, $60$ min $= 1$ h, $24$ h $= 1$ day, $7$ days $= 1$ week, $12$ months $= 1$ year $= 365$ days ($366$ in a leap year).
Part of an hour $\times 60 =$ minutes: $0.4$ h $= 24$ min.
24-hour clock: for p.m. add $12$ to the hour, except from noon to 1 p.m. From midnight to 1 a.m. the hour is $00$.
Time intervals: count on to the next hour, then whole hours, then minutes.
Time zones: ahead, add; behind, subtract. Add the journey first, then change zone, then check the day.

mistakes: Subtracting times as decimals, as in $16.10 - 10.55$. Count on from the start time instead.
Writing $60$ or more minutes, such as $21\,92$. Swap each $60$ minutes for $1$ hour.
Adding p.m. or "hr" to a 24-hour time. Write just the four digits, such as $16\,25$.
Leaving $25\,15$, or the old day, past midnight. Take away $24$ hours: $01\,15$ the next day.
Reading $\tfrac{1}{4}$ hour as $25$ minutes. Multiply by $60$: it is $15$ minutes.
examTips: For a 24-hour time, write four digits, such as $07\,05$, with no a.m. or p.m.
"Work out … in hours and minutes": answer in that form, with under $60$ minutes.
If the question asks for the day and time, give both: the day can earn its own mark.
